Hi Priyom,

Quick question on behalf of one of our APAC resellers (CloudResellCo) — they are seeing withholding being applied by AWS when a US customer purchases through the AWS Marketplace. The downstream invoice shows the marketplace as the seller-of-record and then Amazon deducts a WHT amount before settlement to the reseller.

Two asks: 1) what evidence does Redwood need (W-8/W-9/foreign tax residency docs) so that AWS/Marketplace can avoid or reduce US WHT for a non-US reseller, and 2) is there any way for us to have invoice routing changed so the reseller (not the end-customer) is the billed entity for Redwood usage (i.e., avoid double VAT/WHT complications)?

Reseller details: CloudResellCo (Singapore entity), GST reg #: 2026SG12345, contact: me (Amanda). I can gather docs if you tell me exactly what AWS/Azure/GCP will require.

Priyom / Amanda — quick provider-specific notes (summary):

AWS Marketplace
- AWS generally treats Marketplace as the seller-of-record; the marketplace remits to the seller and may apply US WHT where the seller is treated as US-sourced. To avoid WHT on settlements to a non-US seller, AWS accepts a W-8BEN-E for the foreign entity and (in some cases) a documented tax residency certificate.
- For invoice reallocation (have reseller billed directly for Redwood consumption), AWS requires a supported reseller path (often reseller-led listings or private offers); this typically needs pre-approval and an entity mapping on the AWS side.

Azure Marketplace
- Microsoft can support reseller billing models where the marketplace partner is the transacting party; they require partner billing IDs and tax docs.

GCP / Partner Intermediaries
- GCP has fewer direct marketplace reseller routes; reallocation often requires contract amendments and a billing relationship with the reseller.

Attachments: reseller-invoice-checklist.xlsx (checklist of docs to collect per provider).

I'll prepare a short bullet playbook for each provider we can share with Amanda. If the reseller can get the signed W-8BEN-E + local GST cert, we can open provider tickets to request invoice reallocation / evidence acceptance.

Amanda — thanks for the docs. A few operational notes from finance: 

1) Evidence packet we will submit to AWS/Azure: signed W-8BEN-E, local tax/GST registration, and a reseller declaration letter (short PDF confirming entity role and bank settlement details).

2) AWS path: open a seller support ticket referencing the Marketplace Seller ID and attach the evidence packet. We will request a settlement review and application of treaty/exemption if applicable. If AWS already remitted with WHT, the remedy is typically a refund/credit via Amazon (timeframe varies).

3) Invoice reallocation: if AWS approves mapping the consumption to the reseller entity, we will request a post-issuance credit memo on the Redwood line items so that the reseller can receive the appropriate invoice (this is a manual settlement operation on our side; see internal-invoice-routing-note.pdf). Expect 4–8 weeks for resolution depending on provider responsiveness.

4) Internal ask for Redwood: please confirm the reseller bank payout entity name and tax ID so we can include it in the ticket. Also confirm if the reseller wants Redwood to issue any direct credit memos once provider confirms.
